name: Every operator and verifier list change is audited
summary: operators add|remove and verifiers add|remove take --actor OPERATOR and --reason TEXT (at most 400 characters); restore-new takes both for its --restore-operators/--restore-verifiers re-grants. A real change appends one entry - at, operator, list, actor, change, reason - to the runtime-level authority-changes.audit.json beside deployment.private.json (schema_version 1, mode 0600, 200 entries kept), under the lock and BEFORE the configuration. Every NEW history begins with a compact baseline holding the lists as they stood, and entries the cap drops are folded into a fresh one, so a listed-but-never-mentioned name really is a hand edit or an older kit. The read-only authority-changes prints the entries, the lists, the baseline, the .damaged-* files and the replay; replay.agrees is true, false, or null (no trail yet); the exit code is 0 either way. A damaged audit never refuses a REMOVAL: the bytes are kept beside it first and the new history replaces the path, never leaving it absent; an add that would change something is refused before the lock (a no-op add is not), naming a real .damaged-<stamp>. NOT covered: a hand edit of deployment.private.json; a list change by an older kit.
